ORDO    FOR RECITING
 THE DIVINE OFFICE AND CELEBRATING THE MASS
         ACCORDING TO THE CALENDAR
           OF THE UNIVERSAL CHURCH
                     AND
THE USE OF THE WESTERN RITE VICARIATE GENERAL
                      OF
    THE ANTIOCHIAN ORTHODOX CHRISTIAN
        ARCHDIOCESE OF NORTH AMERICA


           Pro Anno Domini MMXXVI




          ORTHODOX CHRISTIAN PRESS
                    © 2025

NOTE:
This ORDO contains the official liturgical calendar and rubrics for both the Mo-
nastic Breviary and English Office, as well as the Mass according to the Rites of St
Gregory and St Tikhon, as these are published in the Western Rite Vicariate of
the Antiochian Orthodox Christian Archdiocese of North America.
The table of Psalms and Scriptural Readings for Matins and Vespers as found
herein are from “The Lessons for the Christian Year” (1928) and “Psalms and Les-
sons for the Christian Year” (1945) as published in “The Book of Common Prayer”
by the Protestant Episcopal Church in the United States of America. The former
is authorized for use by clergy of the Western Rite Vicariate who make use of “The
English Office” in public worship. The latter is provided for the sake of private
devotion or lectio divina.
We beg the reader’s indulgence for any errors or if certain aspects seem incomplete.

RUBRICS

                                   ANNUAL BLESSINGS
On the following days, either in connection with the Mass, or at another time, and where it is
the custom, the following blessings from the Ritual are to be conferred. When in doubt, the
presumption is in favor of conferral. Blessings marked with an asterisk (*) are obligatory for
pastors and religious superiors.
  *EVERY SUNDAY – The Asperges and Pain Benit.
  *THE EPIPHANY (Jan.6) – Blessings of Chalk, Gold, Incense, Homes, Water (on the
       Vigil).
  *THE PURIFICATION OF THE BVM (Feb. 2) – Blessing of Candles and Procession.
  *ST. BLAISE (Feb. 3) – Blessing of Candles, Bread, Wine, Fruit and Throats.
  HOLY SATURDAY AND IN EASTERTIDE – Blessing of Homes.
  EASTER DAY – Blessing of Lamb, Eggs, Bread, New Produce and Oil.
  HOLY CROSS DAY (May 3), or following Sunday – Crosses for placing in fields, vine-
       yards, gardens and etc.
  NATIVITY OF ST. JOHN BAPTIST (June 24) – Blessing of Bonfires.
  ASSUMPTION OF THE BVM (Aug. 15) – Blessings of Herbs, Fruits, and Flowers.
  NATIVITY OF THE BVM (Sept. 8) – Blessing of Seeds and Seedlings.
  ST. JOHN, APOSTLE AND EVANGELIST (Dec. 27) – Blessing of Wine.

                                         THE MASS
1. On any unimpeded feria, it is permitted to celebrate the Mass of any Saint or Feast listed in
   the Martyrology for that respective day.
2. This Ordo presumes that
       a. The Ordinary of the Mass shall follow “The Ordinary & Canon of the Mass” for
            the Rite of St Gregory as approved by Metropolitan PHILIP in 2012, or St.
            Tikhon's Canon as published by the Vicariate in 1977.
       b. The Propers of the Mass shall follow the text of the English Missal, 1958. The
            pre-1955 form of Holy Week is recommended as being the ancient Western tra-
            dition, but the post-1955 form of Holy Week may be used depending on pastoral
            circumstances.
3. This Ordo presumes that at least three Collects, Secrets and Postcommunion prayers
   (CSP) should be said at every Mass on days below the rank of Double Rite.
   a. The rubrics for the three CSP are as follows. The first CSP is for the Sunday. The sec-
       ond CSP is for the commemoration of a coinciding feast day or octave; and if there are
       none, then the appropriate second seasonal CPS is used. The third CSP is for an addi-
       tional commemoration of a coinciding feast day; and if there are none, then the appro-
       priate second or third seasonal CPS is used.
   b. When the CSP for the Metropolitan is permitted, these prayers are usually labeled
       “For the Pope” (or “For the Chief Bishop”) in Roman and Anglican books. In Sacra-
       mentaries of the 10th century outside of Rome, these particular prayers were applied
       to bishops in general, not specifically to for the Pope.
4. Private or solitary Masses are strictly forbidden. At least one server, or someone to make
   the necessary respones, should be present at each Mass.
5. Mass shall not be celebrated earlier than one hour before sunrise nor later than one hour
   after noon except on Easter, Christmas or with special faculties. Mass at evening shall fol-
   low the general rubrics of the Archdiocese.
6. This Ordo presumes that the bread used for the Mass shall be leavened hosts.
7. This Ordo presumes that the vestments in use in the Western Patriarchate in 1950 shall
   be worn.
8. Mass is never to be celebrated in a private setting without faculties in each instance.

THE DIVINE OFFICE
1. Monastics are bound to the daily recitation of the Breviarium Monasticum. Clergy above
   the order of deacon are bound to the daily recitation of so much of the Breviarium Monas-
   ticum as in their discretion they are able to say.
   a. In addition to the original text, the office may be said or sung from The Monastic Diur-
       nal, Oxford, 1957, and The Monastic Breviary: Matins, Society of the Sacred Cross,
       Tynmawr, 1961.7
2. This Ordo presumes that no other Breviary texts are to be used in the private or public rec-
   itation of the office.
3. All those obliged to the recitation of the divine office (members, oblates and novices of all
   religious communities) who can recite Matins from the Monastic Breviary are urged to do
   so. Those who are unable to recite Matins entire would do well to read at least the lections
   provided in the proper of the season or the saints.

                                  FASTING & ABSTINENCE
1. The instances for fasting and abstinence listed in this Ordo are according to the revised
   Fasting Norms submitted to Metropolitan SABA for his approval.
2. The EUCHARISTIC FAST consists of taking no food or drink (excepting water and med-
   icines) from midnight until the reception of the Eucharist the next morning.
   a. If the Eucharist is to be received at a Mass celebrated in the evening, the Eucharistic
        Fast may be modified as follows: the communicant takes his midday meal as close to
        noon as possible and then takes no food or drink (excepting water and medicines) un-
        til the reception of the Eucharist.

                                       VOTIVE MASSES
1. A Votive Mass, strictly speaking, is one that is celebrated outside of the order of the Office.
   It is called Votive because it is celebrated ex voto, or out of devotion, either of the Celebrant
   or of him who requires or permits it. In a more extended sense, a Votive Mass does not con-
   form to the Office of the Day but is prescribed by the Rubrics. In this sense, a Votive Mass
   is the Mass of a Feast celebrated on the following Sunday to which the External Solemnity
   is transferred; or a Requiem Mass celebrated apart from the day of death or burial; or a
   Nuptial Mass.
2. In either case the choice of rite is not left entirely to the Celebrant’s discretion; he is bound
   to use one of the special forms provided for the purpose at the end of the Missal, or the
   Mass of a canonized Saint on a day other than that Saint’s own feast; but in the latter case
   it is not forbidden to say a Votive Mass more festivo (in the manner of a feast) of a Saint
   (whose name is listed in the Missal or the Vicariate calendar or the Martyrology), on his
   own day provided the Mass is not superseded by a higher rite excluding Votives. The ser-
   vice of a Sunday may not be used as a Votive.
   a. Certain Masses (e.g. of our Lord or of our Lady, &c.) of which the rubrics do not specify
        “In Votive Masses” or “For certain Places” (except in those places where the feast in
        question is observed) are debarred as Votives.
3. Two PrivilegedVotive Masses appointed annually are: (i) The Mass of American Inde-
   pendence Day (July 4) and (ii) the Mass of Thanksgiving Day (fourth Thursday in Novem-
   ber).
        a. On Independence Day (July 4), any Votive Mass may be said, but the Mass of
              Christ the King is most fitting. The color is white, and the Gloria in excelsis and
              Creed are said. The occurrent feasts are commemorated in the CSP. The Preface
              proper to the feast is said.
        b. On the Day of National Thanksgiving, the Mass of the Blessed Sacrament
              (white) or of the Holy Ghost appointed for Thursdays (red) is most fitting. The
              Gloria in excelsis is said, but not the Creed. For the first CSP, that from the Missal
              for Thanksgiving (“O God, who whose mercies there is no number”) is added to

that of the Mass under one concludsion. Occurrent feasts are commemorated in
            the 2nd CSP; no third CSP. The Preface proper to the Mass is said.
4. The Nuptial Mass, for bride and bridegroom, is permitted on many days when other clas-
   ses of Votives are disallowed. However, the Nuptial Mass is prohibited:
   a. On all Sundays
   b. On Doubles of the First or Second Class
   c. During the “closed seasons” (that is, in Advent and Lent)
   d. During the privileged Octaves of Epiphany, Easter, Pentecost, Corpus Christi
   e. On the Vigils of Epiphany and Pentecost;
   f. On All Souls Day, and the Rogation Days.
   g. But on impeded days (except All Souls), even in the closed seasons, if the Ordinary
       gives permission, commemoration of the Nuptial Mass may be made in the Mass of the
       day and the solemn nuptial blessing given.
5. NOTE: The Sacrament of Holy Matrimony, apart from the Nuptial Mass, may be con-
   ducted on any day, including those above, with these exceptions:
   h. September 14: The Elevation of the Cross
   i. December 20-25: The final period of the Advent Fast & the Feast of the Nativity
   j. January 5: The Paramon of Theophany
   k. Great Lent and Holy Week: that is, Ash Wednesday through Easter Saturday
   l. The Sunday of Pentecost
   m. August 1-14: The (Byzantine Rite) Dormition Fast
   n. August 29: The Beheading of St John the Baptist
6. Tables describing the rubrics for various Votive Masses are provided in the opening pages
   of this Ordo.

NOTES FOR EACH LITURGICAL SEASON
Per Annum (Throughout the Year)
Office Notes
„ On Sundays, from January 14 through Quinquagesima Sunday, and from the Sunday nearest Octo-
  ber 1st through the Last Sunday after Pentecost, the Sunday Lauds hymn "Maker of all, eternal King"
  is said (unless the Sunday is superceded by a Double I or Double II Feast).
„ On Sundays, from the Second Sunday after Pentecost until the Sunday nearest October 1st, the Sun-
  day Lauds hymn “Lo! The dim shadows” is said, (unless the Sunday is superceded by a Double I or
  Double II Feast).
„ During Vespers and Lauds, after the Octave of the Epiphany until until Passion Sunday, and after the
  Octave of Pentecost until Advent, the Suffrage of the Saints is said on all Sundays, Ferias and Vigils
  unless there is a commemoration of a any Double Feast or of some Octave. When the Saturday Of-
  fice of the BVM is said, the Suffrage of the Saints proper to that office is said.
„ The final Antiphons of the BVM are said according to the various seasons as noted in the Diurnal.
  These antiphons are said out of Choir, with their versicles and collects, only at the end of Compline,
  Matins (when separated from Lauds), Lauds and Vespers. But in Choir, they are always said at the
  end of every Hour.
„ The final Antiphons of the BVM are said kneeling, except on Sundays (at both I Vespers and II Ves-
  pers) and throughout the entirety of Paschaltide, the Officiant alone rising at the Collect.
Mass Notes
„ On the first free day of each month in which the Ferial Office is said (except in November, December
  17-23, any Ember Day, and all Vigils), a daily (quotidianae) Requiem Mass may be celebrated. And
  on that day in all non-requiem Low Masses, the Collect “For All the Faithful Departed” should be
  added, in the last place but one, to all others required.
„ Likewise, on the Monday of each week in which the Ferial Office is said (out of Lent and Paschaltide),
  commemoration of the dead should be made in all ferial (non-requiem) Low Masses, by the addition
  to the Collects of the day of the Collect “For All the Faithful Departed.” Requiem Mass, however, may
  be said if desired, when so allowed by the rubrics.
„ In all Sunday and Masses of Ferial, Semidouble or Simple Rite and on Vigils and within Octaves, the
  2nd and 3rd CSP is to be said according to the rubrics. The ad libitus prayers are chosen from the “Var-
  ious Prayers to the said at Choice according to the rubrics” near the end of the Missal.
„ On all Sundays without exception, the Asperges me is sung, and its attendant ceremony performed,
  immediately before the beginning of the Mass. During Paschaltide, the Asperges me is replaced with
  the Vidi Aquam.
Christ Mass Tide
„ From the Vigil to the Octave Day of Christmas inclusive, private Votive Masses and Requiem Masses
  are prohibited. Funeral Masses are permitted, except on Christmas Day.
„ During Christmastide, it is appropriate for the Priest to bless infants and children.
Epiphany
„ At High Mass, a genuflexion is made at the words “They fell down and worshipped him” during the
  chanting of the Gospel by the Deacon, not while the Celebrant reads it privately.
„ It is proper on Epiphany Day, or on the Sunday in the Octave, for the solemn announcement of the
  movable feasts of the new year. This is done with a specially appointed chant after the Holy Gospel
  of the day in the principal Mass by a Priest or Deacon vested in cope without stole over his surplice.
  The text of the announcement is located before January 6.
„ On the Feast of the Epiphany, the Priest may bless chalk as well as gold, incense and myrrh. Also,
  throughout Epiphanytide, it is customary for the Parish Priest to bless the homes of the faithful. The
  texts for these rites are in the Orthodox Ritual.
„ At the discretion of the pastor, the Feast of the Holy Family may displace the Sunday within the Oc-
  tave of Epiphany. In this case, the 2nd CPS would be of the Sunday, and the 3rd CSP would be of the
  Octave; and the last Gospel would be from the displaced Sunday.
Candlemas
„ Before the principal Mass, the Blessing of Candles and the Procession take place. At the Blessing
  and the Procession, the color of the vestments and antependium of the altar is violet (this antepen-
  dium is removed after the Procession). The Celebrant wears alb, stole, and cope; the Sacred

NOTES FOR EACH LITURGICAL SEASON
  Ministers wear folded chasubles, or alb without dalmatics; all without the maniple. The altar is not
  adorned with flowers or other ornaments, and the organ is silent until the end of the Procession.
„ The Candles are held lighted in Choir during the singing of the Gospel, and from the Consecration to
  the end of the Communion. The Celebrant at Solemn Mass holds a candle during the chanting of the
  Gospel, and lays it aside before he kisses the book.
„ In small churches, all is observed as in the Memoriale Rituum (the substance of these directions
  may be found in Fortescue’s Ceremonies of the Roman Rite Described).
St Blaise Day
„ On February 3, in honor of St Blaise, the Priest may bless throats with blessed candles. Two candles
  in the “X” position are held before the throats of persons kneeling at the Communion rail as the Cel-
  ebrant says,
     May God free thee from illness of the throat and any other illness through the intercession of
     the Holy Bishop and Martyr Blaise, in the Name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy
     Ghost. ∫ Amen.
Epiphany VII & VIII
„ When the date of Easter is based on Byzantine Paschal calculations using the Julian calendar, there
  can be as many as eight Sundays after Epiphany. When this occurs, there are between twenty-one
  and twenty-three Sundays after Pentecost. Therefore, when there are more than six Sundays after
  the Epiphany, the unused Offices and Masses for the Sundays after Pentecost are anticipated after
  the Sixth Sunday after the Epiphany.
„ FOR THE MASS: When there are seven Sundays after the Epiphany, on the seventh Sunday the
  chants of the Third Sunday after the Epiphany are repeated, and the prayers and lections from the
  Mass for the Twenty-Third Sunday after Pentecost are anticipated on the Seventh Sunday. When
  there are eight Sundays after the Epiphany, on the seventh and eighth Sundays the chants of the
  Third Sunday after the Epiphany are repeated, and the prayers and lections from the Mass for the
  Twenty-Second Sunday after Pentecost are anticipated on the Seventh Sunday after the Epiphany,
  and the prayers and lections from the Mass for the Twenty-Third Sunday after Pentecost are antici-
  pated on the Eighth Sunday after the Epiphany.
„ FOR THE OFFICE: When there are seven Sundays after the Epiphany, the office of the Seventh Sun-
  day is that of the Twenty-Third Sunday after Pentecost. When there are eight Sundays after the
  Epiphany, the office of the Seventh Sunday is that of the Twenty-Second Sunday after Pentecost,
  and the office of the Eighth Sunday is that of the Twenty-Third Sunday after Pentecost.
Septuagesimatide
Office Notes
„ At I Vespers of Septuagesima Sunday, the double Alleluia is added to “Let us bless the Lord.” Hence-
  forward, Alleluia is not said until Holy Saturday at the conclusion of the Vigil.
„ At the beginning of each hour, where Alleluia was said, there is said in its place “Praise be to thee, O
  Lord, King of eternal glory.”
„ The Ferias of the time after Septuagesima are Privileged Ferias of the III Class. Therefore, after Sep-
  tuagesima until Ash Wednesday, the Ferial Office is always said, unless there occurs any Double
  Feast or a day within an Octave; in which case the Feria is commemorated at Lauds (Ant. & = from
  Psalter, with Collect of the preceding Sunday), Mass, and Vespers (proper Ant. & = from Psalter).
„ The Antiphons on Benedictus are said on Ferias as set forth in the Psalter, through Tuesday after
  Quinquagesima. But at Vespers on Ferias, the Antiphons on Magnificat are proper.
Mass Notes
„ In all Masses of Sundays, Feast Days, or Votives until Easter, the Tract is said after the Gradual in
  place of Alleluia and its verse. Gloria in excelsis is not said in seasonal Masses, and the dismissal
  “Let us bless the Lord” (Benedicamus Domino) is said in place of “Depart in peace” (Ite missa est).
„ The colour both of Sundays and weekdays is violet, but dalmatic and tunicle continue to be worn;
  flowers may still be used; and the organ is played as usual.
„ On all Ferias until Ash Wednesday, the Mass of the preceding Sunday is repeated, but without the
  Tract. But “private” Low Masses may be said of a Memorial with Commemoration of the Feria.
„ From Septuagesima through the Tuesday after Quinquagesima, in all Masses which are not of the
  Feria, except Masses for the Dead, Commemoration of the Feria is made.

NOTES FOR EACH LITURGICAL SEASON
„ On the two Saturdays after Septuagesima and Sexagesima, the Conventual Mass may be said of our
  Lady on Saturday, although the Office must be said of the Feria.
Ash Wednesday
„ Before the principal Mass, the Blessing and Imposition of Ashes is made from the blessed palms of
  the preceding year. The Celebrant wears a violet cope.
„ In small churches, all is observed as in the Memoriale Rituum (the substance of these directions
  may be found in Fortescue’s Ceremonies of the Roman Rite Described).
„ For the convenience of the faithful, it is permitted to bless ashes in the early morning, apart from the
  Mass, and they may be imposed at any time by a Priest in surplice and Violet stole; or in the Mass
  vestments immediately before or after a Low Mass. In this case, a Priest in surplice and Violet stole
  performs the blessing with the four prayers prescribed in the Missal, sprinkling but not censing the
  ashes; but the priest in these circumstances must not impose the ashes on himself. Further, on the
  First Sunday in Lent (presuming the solemn blessing and distribution on Ash Wednesday), the
  blessed ashes may be distributed in parish churches in order that the faithful, hindered on Ash
  Wednesday, may avail themselves of this salutary sacramental. The formula “Remember, O man”
  &c. is said over each person while imposing the ashes, but no other form of service of provided.
„ Ashes left over should be thrown into the piscina; none should be preserved.
Lent
Office Notes
„ The first day of Lent is Ash Wednesday, but liturgically the Lenten order of the Office does not begin
  until Vespers of the following Saturday, and the Office hymns for the intervening days are those ap-
  pointed for weekdays as previously.
„ Throughout Lent, in Masses and Offices of the season (except on the IV Sunday), the altar may not
  be adorned with flowers or other ornaments, and the organ is silent (except it be necessary to sus-
  tain a weak choir).
„ From Ash Wednesday, all Octaves cease until Low Sunday inclusive.
„ On Ash Wednesday and the other Ferias until None of Saturday, all is said as in the Psalter, except
  what is appointed in the Proper. After this, all is said as given in the Proper of the Season.
„ On all Lenten Ferias, until Wednesday in holy Week, in Choir, the Preces at Prime and Compline, the
  Pater Noster before the Collect, and the Collect or Collects at all the hours are said kneeling.
„ On Lenten Ferias, the Collect of Lauds is said at all the hours through None. (The second Collect
  given in the Proper for each Feria is said only at Vespers.)
„ The Ferias of Lent and Passiontide are Privileged Ferias of the II Class. Therefore, in the Office,
  Greater and Lesser Doubles and Memorials are merely commemorated during Lent.
„ The Saturday Office of the BVM is never said in Lent.
Mass Notes
„ During the whole of this season, which includes Passiontide, flowers should not adorn the altars and
  the organ should not be played (except on the 4th Sunday) unless it be necessary to sustain a weak
  choir; voluntaries and interludes should be rigorously eschewed; the color is purple; folded chasu-
  bles and the “broad stole” are worn in cathedrals and principal churches (in default, the deacon and
  subdeacon minister in albs — on no account in dalmatic and tunicle).
„ On the 4th Sunday (Lætare), Rose color may be used; tunicles (violet, in defect of rose) are worn; and
  flowers may be used.
„ From Ash Wednesday to Easter Sunday inclusive, the solemn blessing of Marriage and the Nuptial
  Mass are prohibited. But for a just reason the Bishop may permit them.
„ If, on a Lenten Feria, there is a Feast of lower rank than a Double of the II Class, the Priest is at liberty
  (subject to the rubrics) to celebrate the Mass of the Feria, or in lieu thereof, Low Mass of the other
  with the necessary commemoration and prescribed Last Gospel respectively.
„ At Solemn Mass, the Sacred Ministers wear folded chasubles in place of the Dalmatic and Tunicle.
„ Gloria in excelsis is omitted in Masses which are of the Lenten Season, but it is said in Masses for
  Feast Days. The Creed is said on all Sundays and on Feast Days where it is appointed.
„ From Ash Wednesday to Palm Sunday (both inclusive), the Tract always follows the Gradual except
  on such Tuesdays, Thursdays and Saturdays as are Ferias. In the Tract “O Lord, deal not with us after
  our sins”, all kneel at the verse “Help us, O God” (the Sacred Ministers on the edge of the predella)
  while the choir sings it but no one kneels when the Celebrant reads it quietly in a Sung Mass.

NOTES FOR EACH LITURGICAL SEASON
„ The Preface of Lent is said from Ash Wednesday until Saturday before Passion Sunday, inclusive.
„ In Ferial Masses of Lent, there is said “Humble your heads before God” with the proper “Prayer Over
  the People.” (OSP)
„ In Lent, there are no monthly and weekly commemorations of the faithful departed at Mass.
Passiontide
Office Notes
„ Before I Vespers of Passion Sunday, all crosses, including the processional cross (and the Great
  Rood, if accessible) and images, both in church and sacristy, are to be veiled with plain purple cloths
  which must not be transparent. Statues which are part of the architectural features of the building
  and also the Stations of the Cross need not be veiled. The altar candlesticks need not be covered,
  but they may be replaced by others of simpler and less costly character. The veils are not removed
  for any Feast which may occur.
„ In the Office of Passiontide, Gloria Patri is omitted at the end of the Invitatory Psalm at Matins, at the
  end of the last responsory of each Nocturn at Matins, and at the end of each Short Responsory at
  Lauds and Vespers.
„ At Vespers, everyone kneels whilst the verse of the office hymn, “O Cross, our one Reliance, hail!” is
  being sung.
„ From I Vespers of Passion Sunday, through the First Sunday after Pentecost (Trinity Sunday), the
  Suffrage of All Saints is not said at Lauds or Vespers.
Mass Notes
„ From Passion Sunday until Maundy Thursday inclusive (in Masses of the season only) the psalm Ju-
  dica (“Give sentence”) is not said in the Preparation at the beginning of Mass.
„ The Preface of the Holy Cross is said daily until Maundy Thursday, inclusive, unless otherwise noted.
„ In Masses of Passiontide, Gloria Patri is omitted at the Asperges, the Introit, and the psalm Lavabo.
Holy Week (Pre-Schism order)
„ The continuous intent of the Vicariate is the celebration of Holy Week according to the order before
  the liturgical changes by Rome in 1955. In those parishes for which it is a pastoral necessity to use
  the changes instituted by Rome in 1955 and later, the rubrics are located on p. 135-137.
„ From Palm Sunday until Low Sunday inclusive, Private Votive Masses and Masses of Requiem (with
  the exception of Funeral Masses) are prohibited. Funeral Masses, too, are forbidden during the Sa-
  cred Triduum and on Easter Day. Should it happen that a Funeral Mass is requested for a deceased
  person who died, for example, on Wednesday in holy Week and whose burial took place on Good
  Friday, this Mass may be said on the Monday after Easter.
„ Detailed directions for the functions of traditional Holy Week may be found in Fortescue's Ceremo-
  nies of the Roman Rite Described (before the 9th edition). The English text and rubrics of Holy Week
  in traditional form may be found in The English Missal, in editions previous to 1958, or in “Holy Week
  Missal” published by Lancelot Andrewes Press.
„ In small churches, all is observed as in the Memoriale Rituum (the substance of these directions
  may be found in Fortescue’s Ceremonies).
„ The time for the fulfilling of the Paschal Precept (receiving the Holy Communion in one’s own parish
  church) begins on Palm Sunday, and ends on Low Sunday.
Palm Sunday
„ The Asperges is performed before the Blessing of Palms.
„ The Procession is of precept.
„ The blessed palms are held in the hands only during the Procession, and when the Passion and Gos-
  pel are sung.
„ If a Priest has permission from the Ordinary to celebrate two Masses today, he may omit the Passion
  in one (not the principal) Mass. In this Mass the Priest reads the last part of the Passion, beginning
  at Altera autem die (“Now the next day”) in the usual manner of the Gospel. The Last Gospel of this
  Mass is from the Blessing of Palms.
Tenebræ
„ Tenebræ refers to the liturgical Offices of Matins and Lauds as celebrated during the Sacred Trid-
  uum, sung or said by anticipation on the evenings of Wednesday, Thursday and Friday. The English
  text of this service may be found in The Monastic Diurnal (Oxford University Press edition), beginning

NOTES FOR EACH LITURGICAL SEASON
    on p. 285. The music in English may be found in The Monastic Diurnal Noted, Vol. II, beginning on p.
    87. Rubrical and ceremonial directions may be found in Fortescue's Ceremonies of the Roman Rite
    Described.
„   The service must not be held before the altar of repose; nor on Wednesday, before the altar of res-
    ervation unless the Blessed Sacrament is removed before hand.
„   The altar candles, and those in the tenebræ herse, should all be of unbleached wax.
„   On Wednesday at Tenebræ, during the Benedictus, all the lamps throughout the church (except the
    one before the tabernacle) should be extinguished and not relighted until that can be done from the
    new fire blessed on Holy Saturday.
„   In small churches it is permissible to have Tenebræ on one or two only of the evenings.
„   If Matins is celebrated from Lauds in private recitation, the Collect “Almighty God, we beseech thee”
    is added at the end of Matins; and Lauds, after Pater and Ave have been said, is begun with the first
    Antiphon.
Sacred Triduum
„ During the Triduum those who pass before the Cross on the High Altar shall genuflect on one knee,
  with the exception of the Celebrant; and he shall do so likewise after the uncovering of the Cross on
  Good Friday.
„ Except Tenebræ, the Divine Office is not sung, but only monotoned, during these three days. He that
  presides at the Divine Office (even at Tenebræ) wears neither stole nor cope.
„ At all the Hours through None of Holy Saturday, Gloria Patri (“Glory be to the Father”) is omitted at
  the end of the Psalms and in the responsories. The Chapter, Short Responsory, and Hymn are not
  said during the Triduum.
„ Each hour concludes with the Antiphon “Christ for our sake”, the Our Father in secret, the Psalm
  Miserere in a low voice, and the Collect “Almighty God, we beseech thee.”
„ In the sung Office the final verses of the Psalms and Canticles are ended like the others, namely, in
  the ending suited to the Antiphon. When the Office is recited, at all the Hours the voice is lowered a
  tone at the end of each Psalm, Canticle, and division; also at the end of the Psalm Miserere which is
  recited after the Hours in a low tone. The Collect “Almighty God, we beseech thee” is said in a solemn
  monotone, and the last syllable is said in a lower tone, as in the Psalms.
„ During the Triduum, the Martyrology is not read at the end of Prime.
„ At Compline, the Psalms are begun at once; and after the Psalms at once is said the Canticle Nunc
  dimittis; followed by the Antiphon “Christ for our sake” and the rest.
Maundy Thursday
„ According to the traditional order, the Holy Thursday Mass is to be celebrated in the morning. How-
  ever, at the discretion of the pastor and in light of parish custom, the Mass may be celebrated in-
  stead in the evening, i.e., between 4 and 9 p.m.
„ Only one Mass is permitted to be celebrated, and it should be celebrated with all possible dignity and
  solemnity: the best white vestments are worn; the high altar (but this alone) adorned with its most
  costly array; flowers may be used.
„ When the Gloria in excelsis is intoned, the Organ is played and the bells rung; after it they are silent
  until the Gloria on Holy Saturday exclusive. (During this time it is customary to use a wooden clapper
  in place of a bell.)
„ Even at Mass celebrated without Deacon and Subdeacon, the Blessed Sacrament must be in-
  censed at each Elevation
„ The Celebrant consecrates two hosts, of which he consumes one, and reserves the other for the fol-
  lowing day, on which the Sacrament is not consecrated; he also reserves some consecrated parti-
  cles, in case of need, for the sick. According to Orthodox practice, the host for Good Friday and the
  particles for the sick (and for those who may receive on Good Friday) must be touched with a small
  amount of the precious Blood.
„ At the end of the function, a priest in surplice and white stole takes the Sacrament reserved for the
  sick to some remote place (the sacristy, or some other seemly chamber outside the body of the
  church), suitably prepared, where It will be kept with a light continuously burning before It, until It is
  brought back at the end of the functions on Holy Saturday. From this time until the Mass of Holy Sat-
  urday, Holy Communion is not distributed, except to the sick as Viaticum; in this case, a white stole
  is worn.
„ After the Solemn Mass, Holy Water is removed from all fonts in the Church.

NOTES FOR EACH LITURGICAL SEASON
„ After the Procession, Vespers are said in Choir with the six candles lighted. After Vespers the Altars
  are stripped, only the Cross and the six candlesticks being allowed to remain. This holds good like-
  wise for the next day. (But if, in any place, Vespers are not said in Choir, the stripping of the Altars
  takes place immediately after the removal of the Ciborium with the Blessed Sacrament.)
„ The ceremony of the Mandatum, or washing of feet, is a rite performed at a convenient hour outside
  the Mass and sanctuary by the Bishop in his cathedral. However, if, by indult, this ceremony is per-
  formed in a Vicariate parish, only the feet of thirteen minor clerics or poor men are washed. The prel-
  ate or priest puts on a violet stole and cope over the amice and alb. Then the deacon, in white vest-
  ments (as is also the subdeacon) sings the Gospel from the Mass. (John 13: 1-15) The officiating
  priest then removes his cope, girds himself with a cloth and, assisted by his ministers begins the
  washing of the feet of the men chosen for the ceremony. The officiating priest kneels before each
  one of them, washes, wipes and kisses the foot presented, using the cloth tendered by the deacon.
  Meanwhile the appointed antiphons are sung.
Good Friday
„ According to the traditional order, the Solemn Liturgy for Good Friday is to be celebrated in the morn-
  ing with Tenebrae prayed in the evening. However, at the discretion of the pastor and in light of par-
  ish custom, the Solemn Liturgy may be celebrated instead at any time between 12 noon and 6 pm,
  with the Tenebrae following shortly thereafter.
„ At the discretion of the pastor and in light of parish custom, the faithful may, during the Liturgy, re-
  ceive Holy Communion from the Reserved Sacrament.
„ The bells and organ remain silent until Gloria in excelsis at the Mass on Holy Saturday.
„ The altar Cross is veiled in violet, not black. At the Presanctified Mass, the Sacred Ministers wear the
  folded chasubles.
„ The customary kisses are omitted, even those of the chalice and paten, but the Celebrant does kiss
  the altar. The Deacon and Subdeacon are not blessed at the Epistle and Gospel; incense is not used
  until the procession; and no one bows to another at any time.
„ The last part of the Passion, which takes the place of the Gospel, is not said on the Gospel side, but
  on the Epistle side, where (not at the middle of the Altar) the Celebrant, bowing profoundly and
  turned toward the Cross, says “Cleanse my heart” without Jube &c. and reads the remaining part of
  the Passion. He does not kiss the Missal.
„ At the Adoration of the Cross the Celebrant and the Sacred Ministers lay aside the maniple, and like-
  wise their shoes.
„ The Procession from the Repository takes place as on the preceding day; the humeral veil worn in
  carrying the Blessed Sacrament (today and always) is white.
„ After the usual incensation of the oblations, the altar Cross and the Altar itself are incensed in the
  usual manner, with the words “May this incense.”
„ At the “Pray, brethren” no response is made.
„ The Celebrant raises the Sacred Host with his right hand only in such a way that It may be seen by
  the faithful, his left hand remaining on the altar. At the elevation the Sacred Ministers do not raise
  the chasuble, nor incense the Blessed Sacrament.
„ After the consuming of the Blessed Sacrament, the lights, or candles, that are carried by the Clergy
  are extinguished. But the six candles upon the Altar are not extinguished until after Vespers.
„ From the Adoration of the Cross on Good Friday until None of Holy Saturday, all, even the Celebrant,
  in passing before the Cross on the main Altar, shall make a genuflexion.
Holy Saturday
„ According to the traditional order, the ceremonies of the Paschal Vigil are to take place in the morn-
  ing. However, at the discretion of the pastor and in light of parish custom, the Vigil may be celebrated
  instead at a convenient hour in the afternoon or evening.
„ The usual salutations in choir are resumed today; as also the customary kisses.
„ Holy Communion may be given today only in the course of the Mass, or immediately afterwards, not
  before, except by way of Viaticum to the dying.
„ At the ceremonies and the Prophecies the violet color is used. Only the Deacon, when singing the
  Lumen Christi and the Exsultet, wears dalmatic, stole, and maniple of white.
„ If people who are to be baptized are present, especially if there should be many of them, it is permis-
  sible to transfer to a convenient time in the morning of the same day the ceremonies of the Ritual

NOTES FOR EACH LITURGICAL SEASON
    that precede the actual administration of Baptism, namely, in the Baptism of Infants up to the word
    “Do you believe,” and in the Baptism of Adults up the words “What is your name?”.
Paschaltide
Office Notes
„ Throughout Paschaltide until None of Saturday after Pentecost inclusive, at all Offices Alleluia is
  added to all Antiphons when said in their entirety, as well as to all versicles and responsories. But
  Alleluia is not added to the versicles in the Preces of Prime and Compline, nor to Pretiosa (“Right
  dear”) at the end of Prime. Alleluia, alleluia is added to the Short Responsories at Vespers and
  Lauds, as noted in their proper places.
„ The words Alleluia, alleluia are added to “Let us bless the Lord” at the close of Lauds and Vespers,
  only until the Vespers of the Saturday before Low Sunday.
„ All hymns of the same metre have the proper doxology “To thee who, dead, again dost live” through
  None of the Vigil of the Ascension, except those which have their proper ending.
„ The Ordinary of the Ferial Office in Paschaltide is followed for minor Double Feasts and Simple Of-
  fices when the Psalms at Lauds are to be taken from the occurring Feria in the Psalter, as well as
  within the Octave of the Ascension and on Friday after that Octave.
„ During Paschaltide, except on Doubles and within Octaves (including the Easter Octave), the Preces
  are said as in the Psalter.
„ There is no kneeling at the Office in Paschaltide.
„ There are proper Antiphons on Benedictus and Magnificat for each of the Ferias of Paschaltide. The
  Collect is always taken from the preceding Sunday.
„ From Monday after Low Sunday through the Vigil of the Ascension, the common Commemoration of
  the Holy Cross is said in the Semidouble or Simple Office of the Season or of the Saints, except when
  there has been a commemoration of a Double, even in Concurrence, or an Office or commemoration
  of any Octave.
„ The Final Antiphon of the BVM, Regina cæli, is said at the end of the Office through None of Ember
  Saturday in the Pentecost Octave. Likewise, outside the Office, Regina cæli takes the place of the
  Angelus.
„ At Friday Vespers throughout Paschaltide (through the Saturday before the V Sunday after Easter),
  unless a Double Feast or some Octave occurs on the following day, the Office from the Chapter on is
  that of the B.V.M. on Saturday: and that Office is said on the following Saturday.
Mass Notes
„ In the principal Mass of Sundays, Vidi aquam takes the place of Asperges me; it is begun kneeling
  even on Easter Day itself. Water is not blessed on Easter Day and Pentecost if the blessing of water
  has been done in the function on the previous day; the water then blessed is used for the aspersion
  on the Sunday.
„ Gloria in excelsis is said on Feasts and Ferias alike except in Rogation Masses and ordinary Votive
  Masses.
„ The words “Alleluia, alleluia” are added to the Introit; one “Alleluia” to the Offertory verse; and one
  “Alleluia” to the Communion verse.
„ The Gradual is said as usual during the Easter Octave but is omitted on and from Low Saturday, and
  in its place the “Great Alleluia” is said in all Masses of the Season and of the Saints, but not in Roga-
  tion Masses, nor on the Vigil of Pentecost.
„ The Easter Preface is said in all Masses until the Ascension, except in that of a Feast having a proper
  Preface.
„ Throughout Paschaltide, the Paschal Candle remains in its candelabrum and should be lighted dur-
  ing Masses and Vespers which are sung; it may be lighted during Low Masses celebrated with some
  solemnity, as well as during other liturgical functions, up to the Gospel inclusive of the day of our
  Lord's Ascension, after which it is to be extinguished, and removed from its candelabrum after the
  Mass is finished.
„ In Paschaltide, there are no monthly or weekly commemorations of the faithful departed at Mass.
„ The Priest may bless the homes of the faithful throughout Paschaltide, using the blessed water
  taken from the baptismal font before the infusion of the Sacred Oils. Other traditional blessings on
  Easter Day and throughout the season include: lamb, eggs, bread, new produce, oil, or any other
  kind of food.

The Greater Litany
„ The Rogation Procession is of obligation in cathedral and conventual churches, but not strictly in
  ordinary parish churches; nor, in the latter case, need the Rogation Mass be celebrated except on
  Rogation Monday (when not impeded according to the rubrics).
„ On the Feast of St Mark (April 25), if the procession is held, the Mass of the Rogation is celebrated
  as usual, without Gloria and Credo, but with the commemoration of St Mark and the Preface of
  Easter. Where the procession is not held, the Mass shall always be of the Feast of St Mark, and the
  commemoration of the Rogations is made.
„ Although, as stated, the procession is not of obligation in ordinary parish churches, the Litany of the
  Saints, if at all practicable, should be sung (or recited without chant) in procession before the princi-
  pal Mass; but if the procession cannot be held it is nevertheless desirable and laudable that the Lit-
  any be recited after Lauds (immediately after “Let us bless the Lord,” omitting “May the souls” and
  all that follows including the Marian Antiphon). The Litany may not be anticipated or postponed.
„ But in those churches in which there are several Priests, it is more conformable to the rubrics that
  the Mass of the Rogations also be celebrated, with the Procession; but it is not of strict precept, ex-
  cept in those Churches in which a Conventual Mass must be sung every day.
„ The Greater Litany of the Saints is never transferred unless it falls on Easter Sunday; in which case,
  it is said on Easter Tuesday.
„ “During these three days [before the Feast of the Ascension], those who do not take part in the Ro-
  gation Processions are to say privately after lauds the Litany with the Preces and Collects, but with-
  out the Penitential Psalms.” (MD, 387)
May Devotions in Honor of Our Lady
„ In many Churches, the month of May is especially dedicated to the BVM, and celebrated with suita-
  ble practices of devotion.
„ In those Churches in which there is a side altar dedicated to the BVM, that altar should be used and
  adorned for these devotions. Where no such altar exists, however, it is quite proper to erect a special
  altar, or shrine, with a statue or picture of the BVM and adorned with candles and flowers. But it is
  not proper to expose the image under a canopy.
„ If the exercises of the May devotion take place at the altar of the BVM, and at the end the Blessed
  Sacrament is to be exposed for Benediction, this should be done at the main altar, where the
  Blessed Sacrament is reserved.
Vigil of Pentecost
„ The ceremonies of the Solemn Blessing of the Font may be performed, including the six Prophecies,
  Litany of the Saints, and the Mass.
„ The Celebrant and sacred ministers are robed in violet vestments, and the candles on the altar are
  not lighted until the beginning of Mass, as on Holy Saturday.
„ At the end of each of the six Prophecies, a Tract is sung and a Collect read, but “Let us bow the knee”
  is not said. At the end of the Prophecies, the Celebrant puts on a violet cope, and while the proces-
  sion moves toward the font, the Tract Sicut cervus (“As the hart”) is sung. The Font is blessed, as on
  Holy Saturday. Where there is no Font, the Litany begins after the Prophecies and Collects.
„ The Litany of the Saints is sung, as on Holy Saturday; and at the verse “We sinners” the Priest and
  his assistants go to the sacristy and put on the red vestments, and the candles are lit on the altar. At
  the end of the Litany, Kyrie eleison is sung solemnly, without Introit, as on Holy Saturday. At the Glo-
  ria, the bells are also rung and the organ begins being played.
„ Where these ceremonies are not performed, a simple Mass of the Vigil may be said, with the Introit
  Cum sanctificatus.
The Feast of Pentecost
„ The Feast of Pentecost is the second greatest feast of the year, and its Octave has precisely the
  same rank and privileges as are attached to that of Easter and should be celebrated with equal
  splendor and solemnity.
„ The color is red throughout the week, including the Ember Days, the Octave ceasing before the 1st
  Vespers of Trinity Sunday on which no reference is made to the Feast of Pentecost.
„ In the “Great Alleluia” all genuflect while the verse “Come, Holy Ghost” is being sung, but no one
  kneels while the Priest reads it privately.

NOTES FOR EACH LITURGICAL SEASON
„ At Vespers daily, all kneel whilst the first verse of the Office Hymn Veni Creator is sung. This hymn is
  also said at Terce throughout the whole Octave, instead of the ordinary hymn Nunc Sancte nobis
  Spiritus.
Trinity Sunday
„ Paschaltide ends with None of Saturday before the 1st Vespers of Trinity Sunday; the addition of
  Alleluia to the antiphons is discontinued; the recitation of the text of the Angelus is resumed this
  evening; and that of the Asperges on Trinity Sunday.
„ At Prime, when Gloria Patri has been said at the end of the last portion of the Psalm, then is begun
  immediately the Athanasian Symbol (Quicumque vult). The 23rd verse, in accordance with Eastern
  Orthodox doctrine, should be changed to read: “The Holy Ghost is of the Father through the Son: nei-
  ther made, nor created, nor begotten, but proceeding.”
Corpus Christi
Office Notes
„ The Feast of the Most Holy Body of Christ ranks with the Epiphany in dignity next after Easter and
  Pentecost.
„ At the Verses of the Hymns in the Divine Office, Tantum ergo and O salutaris, all genuflect if the Of-
  fice is recited in Choir before the Blessed Sacrament exposed.
„ In the Hymn Pange lingua, according to Eastern Orthodox doctrine, the final two lines of the last
  Verse must be said thus: “Ever too His love confessing, who from One with Both is One.”
„ The conclusion of the Hymns is of the Nativity during the whole Octave: “All honour, praise, and glory
  be, O Jesu, Virgin-born, to thee.”
Mass Notes
„ On the Sunday within the Octave, one Solemn Mass may be celebrated as on the Feast, with Gloria,
  Sequence, Creed, Preface of the Nativity [or ad lib. Preface of the Blessed Sacrament], commemo-
  ration of the Sunday under a distinct conclusion, and its Gospel as the Last Gospel. Solemn Vespers,
  II Vespers of the Feast, may be celebrated on the Sunday.
„ During this Octave, but not on the Octave Day, the Sequence Lauda Sion may be omitted at Low
  Masses.
„ During the Octave of Corpus Christi, not only private Votive Masses and Low Masses of Requiem are
  prohibited, but also the Requiem High Mass for the first time after death, or after the receipt of the
  news of a death; on the Octave Day are prohibited those Low Masses of Requiem which are other-
  wise allowed on the day, or for the day of death in connection with the Funeral Mass. A Funeral Mass
  is prohibited on the Feast itself; but if the Solemnity is transferred to the Sunday, a Funeral Mass is
  permitted on the Feast. Also, the Votive Nuptial Mass is prohibited during the entire Octave, but a
  Commemoration thereof may be made and the Solemn Nuptial Blessing given.
Procession Notes
„ The Priest first celebrates Mass, during which he consecrates two hosts. After he has consumed the
  one, he mounts the other in the Monstrance which will be carried in the Procession. The part of the
  Monstrance which holds the Host should be encircled with glass, so that the Host is visible to the
  worshippers. (But if the Procession is transferred to the Sunday within the Octave, the Blessed Sac-
  rament may be exposed at the beginning of the Mass, and after the Mass the Procession is held.)
„ When Mass is over and the Procession has already started, the Priest, vested in white cope, will in-
  cense the Blessed Sacrament with threefold incensation, the while he kneels. Then one of the as-
  sisting clergy places a suitable Humeral veil over the Priest's shoulders. The latter, covering both
  hands with the ends of the veil, reverently receives the Monstrance which is handed to him by the
  Deacon. Holding the Blessed Sacrament before his face, he turns toward the people and joins the
  Procession, waLk ing beneath the canopy with his ministers escorting him. Before him walk two ac-
  olytes or clerics carrying thuribles with burning incense. All march with bared heads, holding lighted
  candles, and devoutly singing the Hymns appointed, as the length of the Procession will permit. As
  soon as the Priest leaves the altar, either he himself or the clergy intone the Hymn Pange lingua.
„ The psalms, hymns, and prayers for the Procession may be found in the supplement.
„ At the end of the Procession, when the Blessed Sacrament has been brought back to the church and
  placed on the altar, all the clergy as they kneel in reverent adoration sing the last stanza of Tantum
  ergo, during which the Priest incenses the Blessed Sacrament at the usual time. Two clerics sing the
  Versicle and Response (“Thou givest them”), and the Priest rises to say the prayer. Having made a

NOTES FOR EACH LITURGICAL SEASON
  genuflection, the Priest blesses the people with the Monstrance, making a single Sign of the Cross
  and without saying anything. Lastly, the Blessed Sacrament is reposed in the tabernacle.
„ Note that, in the Procession, the Sacred Ministers properly wear either surplice and stole, or chasu-
  bles, or copes, of white, but not dalmatics.
„ The Procession may take place in the evening, either on the Feast, on the Sunday, or sometime dur-
  ing the Octave
October Devotions in Honor of Our Lady
„ It is a pious and laudable custom, that from Oct. 1 to Nov. 2 inclusive, in all Parish Churches and
  Oratories, at least Five Decades of the Rosary, with the Litany of the Blessed Virgin Mary and a spe-
  cial Prayer in honor of St Joseph (see below), her Spouse, should be recited daily either in the morn-
  ing during the Holy Sacrifice of the Mass, or at another time before the Blessed Sacrament exposed.
  The texts for this devotion can be found until the title “The October Devotions” in the Appendix to the
  Orthodox Ritual.
„ If the solemn exposition with the Ostensorium is impossible, it is possible to have this exposition with
  the Ciborium, namely, by opening the door of the Tabernacle while reciting these prayers, and at the
  end blessing the faithful with the Ciborium.
„ The Prayer in Honor of St Joseph:
      To thee, O blessed Joseph, we have recourse in our tribulations, and while imploring the aid
      of thy most holy Spouse, we confidently invoke thy patronage also. By that love which united
      thee to the Spotless Virgin, Mother of God, and by the fatherly affection with which thou didst
      embrace the Infant Jesus, we humbly beseech thee graciously to regard the inheritance
      which Jesus Christ purchased with his Blood and to help us in our necessities, by thy power-
      ful intercession. Protect, O most provident Guardian of the Holy Family, the chosen children
      of Jesus Christ; ward off from us, O most loving Father, all taint of error and corruption; gra-
      ciously assist us from heaven, O most power protector, in our struggle with the powers of
      darkness; and as thou didst once rescue the Child Jesus from imminent peril to his life, so
      now defend the Holy Church of God from the snares of her enemies and from all adversity.
      Shield each one of us with thy unceasing patronage that, imitating thy example and sported
      by thy aid, we may be enabled to live a good life, die a holy death, and secure everlasting hap-
      piness in heaven. ∫ Amen.
All Souls' Day
Office Notes
„ Because the Faithful Departed are commemorated on November 2, the monthly commemoration
  of the departed is omitted in November.
„ At II Vespers of All Saints, the Vespers of the Dead are begun immediately after “Let us bless the
  Lord.” The Our Father and Hail Mary are not said unless, out of Choir, Vespers of the Dead were sep-
  arated from Vespers of the preceding Feast; Vespers of the Dead are begun immediately with the
  Antiphon “I will walk.”
„ The Antiphons at Vespers, as well as at Matins and Lauds, are said in their entirety before and after
  each Psalm and Canticle.
„ Compline begins immediately with the Confiteor, followed by the usual Psalms without an Antiphon.
  The Canticle of Simeon, Nunc dimittis, is said immediately after the Psalms.
„ At the end of each Psalm is said: “Rest eternal grant unto them, O Lord. And let light perpetual shine
  upon them.”
„ All is said as in the common Office of the Dead, except those things that are noted in the Proper of
  the Saints under November 2.
„ The Office of All Souls' is ended with the celebration of Mass after None. Vespers are of the Octave
  of All Saints.
Mass Notes
„ Only one Mass is authorized or allowed on All Souls Day. The Mass that comes first in the Missal (its
  intention for “all the faithful departed”) must be used; and for a funeral taking place that day.
„ Before the Mass a catafalque, with lighted candles around it (four or six; more are allowed), should
  be set up in the position outside the chancel it usually occupies, for the solemn Absolution of the
  Dead, which should follow at the end of the Mass.

NOTES FOR EACH LITURGICAL SEASON
„ Unbleached wax candles are generally used; vestments and altar vesture are black; but if the Sac-
  rament is reserved and cannot be removed, the frontal should be purple even though the vestments
  are black.
„ The Sequence Hymn Dies iræ is to be used entire whether the Mass is sung or said.
„ Communion may be given but the assistant (other than the Sacred Ministers of the Mass) should
  wear a violet stole as would be done if Communion were given today outside Mass.
„ As mentioned above, a funeral may take place today, but in that event the prayers of the funeral
  Mass are added above one conclusion to those appointed for the day. During the seven days follow-
  ing All Souls' Day, a Requiem Mass celebrated by request for any particular soul or souls has all the
  privileges of an anniversary Mass provided it is celebrated with chant.
Office of XXIII Pentecost
„ The Office of the last Sunday after Pentecost is always that of the XXIV Sunday after Pentecost, even
  if sometimes there are only twenty-three Sundays after Pentecost. In this case, the XXIV Sunday is
  put in place of the XXIII Sunday, and the Office of the XXIII is placed on the preceding Saturday. On
  this day, the Collect of the XXIII Sunday is said at Friday Vespers as well as in Matins (II Nocturn),
  Lauds, and the Minor Hours. At Matins, three Lessons are read from the Homily of the Sunday in
  place of the Scriptural Lessons for that Saturday. At Lauds, the Antiphon on the Benedictus is said,
  exactly as given in the Breviary.
Advent
Office Notes
„ All Ferias throughout Advent until the day before the Vigil of the Nativity of our Lord, inclusive, are
  Privileged Ferias of the III Order. On Advent Ferias, the Ferial Office is always said unless there occurs
  any Double Feast or day within an Octave: in which case the Feria is commemorated at Vespers,
  Lauds and Mass.
„ On Ferias in Advent, until December 17, when there are no proper Antiphons at Lauds, the Antiphons
  of the Hours are taken from Lauds of the preceding Sunday. But after December 17, when proper
  Antiphons are appointed for Lauds on Ferias, the Antiphons of the Hours are taken from the same
  Antiphons of Lauds.
„ In the Ferial Office, the Collect of the preceding Sunday is said (except on the Ember Days when the
  Collect is proper).
„ The Suffrage of the Saints is not said in Advent, through the Octave of the Epiphany inclusive
„ In the Ferial Office, the Preces at Prime and Compline are said kneeling.
„ In the Office of the Advent Season, the proper hymn doxology of the BVM, “All honour, laud, and glory
  be, O Jesu, Virgin-born, to thee” is not said.
„ The Marian Antiphon Alma Redemptoris Mater is said from Vespers of the Saturday before the 1st
  Sunday in Advent through II Vespers of the Purification (Feb. 2).
„ Vigils in Advent are commemorated only at Mass, never in the Office.
„ The Saturday Office of the BVM is never said in Advent.
Mass Notes
„ Advent is not a penitential season in the same sense that Lent is, and therefore the use of Alleluia is
  not barred, but the sanctuary and altars should be adorned somewhat more simply and flowers not
  employed except on the 3rd Sunday and Christmas Eve.
„ From the First Sunday in Advent to the Feast of Christmas inclusive, the solemn blessing of Marriage
  and the Nuptial Mass are prohibited. But for a just reason the Bishop may permit them.
„ In Masses of the Advent Season, Gloria in excelsis is omitted, and “Let us bless the Lord” is said for
  the Dismissal. But when Mass is of a Feast, Gloria and “Depart in peace” are said.
„ On Ferias in Advent, when during the week the Sunday Mass is resumed, the Alleluia and its verse
  are not said, but only the Gradual.
„ The Preface of the Most Holy Trinity is said on Sundays in Advent, and the Common Preface is said
  on Advent Ferias. However, the Priest, at his own discretion, may say the ad libitum Preface of Advent
  on Sundays and Ferias in Advent. In Masses of the Advent Season, the Preface of the BVM is never
  said.
„ On Sundays and Ferias of Advent (at Mass and in the Office), the organ should not be played (except
  to support a weak choir), nor should the altar be adorned with flowers, statues, or relics of the Saints.

NOTES FOR EACH LITURGICAL SEASON
„ At Mass, according to the rubrics, the sacred ministers wear the folded chasubles. But if these are
  not at hand, they shall wear the alb, without dalmatic or tunicle.
„ On the Third Sunday in Advent (Gaudete Sunday), vestments of Rose color may be worn; the sacred
  ministers wear dalmatic and tunicle, the organ may be played, and the altars may be decorated with
  flowers. (Also, on the Vigil of the Nativity, the altar may be decorated with flowers.)
„ In order to foster the devotion of the faithful toward the Divine Redeemer, the pious custom has
  been introduced in some churches of celebrating on every day in Advent a Votive High Mass of the
  Blessed Virgin Mary, the so-called “Rorate Mass”, which is the first in order among the Votive
  Masses of the Blessed Virgin. This Mass is said without Gloria (except on Saturday). During the Oc-
  tave of the Conception, the Rorate Mass is suspended in favor of the Octave.
Christ Mass Day
„ The missal provides three Masses for December 25. This is of ancient tradition (5th century). Every
  priest is allowed to celebrate three Masses on Christmas Day. If he says only one or two of them, he
  should do so in their proper order and as near the rubrical Hours as convenient. St Anastasia is com-
  memorated only at the Dawn Mass.
„ Communion may be given at the Midnight Mass. The celebrant and communicants should follow the
  Eucharistic Fast from Vespers (about six hours).
„ The First Vespers of Christmas Day should be said at the ordinary hour and not postponed to near
  midnight. The Midnight Mass is properly preceded only with the Office of Matins (the blessing of the
  Crib might also take place then).
„ When Midnight Mass of Christmas Day is followed immediately by Lauds, the Office begins at once
  with the Versicle Deus in adjutorium. Prime is said in the early morning, after which the 2nd Mass of
  the Nativity is offered at daybreak. Terce is said at an appropriate Hour, after which the 3rd Mass of
  the Nativity is offered.
„ At each Solemn Mass today the Sacred Ministers, if they are at the sedilia, kneel with bowed head
  on the lowest step at the Epistle side, facing liturgical north (or at the sedilia) while the choir sings
  “And was incarnate” in the Creed; or if they are still at the altar they kneel on the edge of the predella.
„ In the Third Mass, no reverence is made during the private reading of the Gospel by the Celebrant;
  but the genuflexion is made as usual when the Deacon comes to the phrase “And the Word was
  made flesh.”
„ At the Third Mass of the Nativity, the Epiphany Gospel is read as the Last Gospel, and a genuflexion
  is made at the words “They fell down and worshipped him.”
„ It is a laudable and widespread custom at Christmastide to erect within the church a representation
  of the birthplace of our blessed Redeemer; or at least to exhibit a figure of the divine Infant (the Bam-
  bino). This figure may be placed in a prominent position on the altar or on a support nearby (but not
  in the throne of exposition, or in place of the cross). At the incensations it is censed by the Priest
  standing, exactly in the same manner as, and after, the altar cross. The Bambino is usually laid in
  the Christmas Crib immediately before or after the Midnight Mass; or if there be no Midnight Mass,
  then as near to midnight as may be convenient. If it is desired to make a ceremony of this by carrying
  the figure in procession (with or without lights and incense) there is no law forbidding it. It is a com-
  mon custom after solemn services in the Christmas season for the Priest in cope, attended by serv-
  ers, to visit the Crib—so many of the congregation as can conveniently do so joining in—where popu-
  lar devotions in honour of the Holy Child are said. If the Bambino is censed it should be done by the
  Priest standing, although the congregation may be kneeling.

RUBRICS FOR CELEBRATING
                             The Patronal or Titular Feast of a Parish
                           The Dedication of a Parish Church (Temple)
1.   Those parish churches and oratories, public or semi-public, which are consecrated, or at least sol-
     emnly blessed, should celebrate annually, with great solemnity, both the Title or Titular Saint, and
     the day of Dedication.
     a. In Byzantine usage, the Titular Saint of a church may be known as the Patronal Saint, and the
            feast may be known as the Patronal feast.
     b. In the Antiochian Archdiocese, the Title is assigned by the Metropolitan Archbishop.
2.   The Feast of the Titular Saint (or Mystery) and the Day of Dedication should be celebrated annually
     on their proper days.
     a. Both Feasts are Primary Double of the First Class with a Common Octave.
     b. Should the Feast of the Titular Saint (or Mystery) occur on another Primary Double of the First
            Class, the Feast of the Titular Saint is translated to the next open day. (See some exceptions
            below).
     c.     The days in the Octave for the Feast of the Titular Saint are Semidoubles.
            i. Should one of the days in the Octave occurs on a Feast of the Double I or Double II Rite or
                 in the Octaves of Easter or Pentecost, the commemoration of the Feast of the Titular
                 Saint is omitted.
           ii. Should one of the days in the Octave occurs on a Feast of the Lesser Double or Greater
                 Double or in the Octaves of Epiphany, Corpus Christi, Nativity of the Lord or Ascension,
                 the Feast of the Titular Saint is commemorated.
          iii. Should one of the days in the Octave occurs on an Ember day, the Feast of the Titular
                 Saint is commemorated.
          iv. When one of the days in the Octave occurs on a Sunday (if the External Solemnities are
                 not transferred), then the Feast of the Titular Saint is commemorated.
           v. Should one of the days in the Octave occurs on a Feria outside of Lent, the Feast of the
                 Titular Saint is repeated, and any memorials are commemorated.
          vi. Should the Feast of the Titular Saint occur during Lent, the Octave and Octave Day are
                 omitted.
     d. The Octave Day for the Feast of the Titular Saint is a Greater Double, and is commemorated
            only when it occurs on a Sunday, a Feast of the Double I or Double II Rite, in Lent, or on the
            Octave of the Epiphany and Corpus Christi.
3.   Within the Octave of the Feast of Title or Dedication:
     a. The Gloria in excelsis and the Creed are said in all the Masses of the Octave or of any Feast
            occurring.
     b. The 2nd CSP is of the Blessed Virgin Mary and the 3rd CSP is for the Church or Metropolitan.
4.   Should the Feast of the Titular Saints (or Mystery) not occur on a Sunday, the External Solemnity of
     the Feast may be transferred, at the pastor’s discretion, to the Sunday following the feast (that is,
     the Sunday within the Octave of the Feast of Title).
     a. When the External Solemnities of the Feast are transferred to the following Sunday, the Mass
            of the Feast is said with the 2 CSP from occuring Sunday only. In addition, the Last Gospel is
            that of the occuring Sunday.
5.   Specific rubrics for the churches in the Vicariate:
     a. The ad lib. Preface of All Saints and Holy Patrons may be used on the Feast of Title only in
            these churches: St Anthony, St Augustine, St Benedict, St Columba, St Gregory, St Nicholas,
            St Patrick and St Vincent.
     b. The Preface of the Apostles must be used on the Feast of Title in these churches: St Andrew,
            St Mark, St Paul, St Peter.
     c.     Other churches must use the Preface assigned to the Feast.

    for Our Lady of Walsingham under the English title.

Holy Week (Post-Schism 1955 Church of Rome rubrics)
„ From Palm Sunday until Low Sunday inclusive, Private Votive Masses and Masses of Requiem
  (with the exception of Funeral Masses) are prohibited. Funeral Masses, too, are forbidden during
  the Sacred Triduum and on Easter Day. Should it happen that a Funeral Mass is requested for a
  deceased person who died, for example, on Wednesday in Holy Week and whose burial took place
  on Good Friday, this Mass may be said on the Monday after Easter.
„ The functions of Holy Week are of obligation in parish churches. In churches and oratories where
  the solemn rite of Holy Week cannot be carried out, the ceremonies may be done in the "simple
  rite" as described in the rubrics.
„ During Holy Week in the revised order, when the ceremonies are carried out in the solemn rite,
  with deacon and subdeacon, whatever is sung (or said) by the deacon, subdeacon, or a lector, in
  virtue of their office, is not duplicated secretly by the Celebrant.
„ During Holy Week, no commemorations are made in the Office or in the Mass. A Double of the 1st
  or 2nd Class is transferred until after Low Sunday; all other feasts are omitted altogether for that
  year.
„ The color for Holy Week is violet, except on Maundy Thursday, when white is worn, and Good
  Friday, when black is worn for part of the function; and red is worn for the palm procession on
  Sunday. The Deacon and Subdeacon wear red dalmatic and tunicle.
„ When the Blessed Sacrament is present on the altar all salute It by a genuflexion. When It is not
  present, the Celebrant salutes the altar and its cross by a low bow, all others by a genuflexion (but
  only during a function). When not even the cross is on the altar (as at the first part of the service
  of Good Friday), all salute the altar, during a function, by the bow of the head only.
„ Detailed directions for the functions of Holy Week (revised order of 1955) may be found in For-
  tescue's Ceremonies of the Roman Rite Described (after the 9th edition). The English text and
  rubrics of Holy Week in the revised rite may be found in The English Missal, 1958 edition.
„ The folded chasubles and the broad stole are not used at any time in Holy Week, according to the
  revised order.
„ On Palm Sunday, and on Monday, Tuesday and Wednesday of Holy Week, the Divine Office is said
  at the usual hours.
„ The time for the fulfilling of the Paschal Precept (receiving the Holy Communion in one’s own
  parish church) begins on Palm Sunday, and ends on Low Sunday.
Notes for Palm Sunday (Post-Schism 1955 Church of Rome rubrics)
„ On this day the solemn blessing of, and procession with, palms in honour of Christ the King, takes
  place normally in the morning after Terce. The color is red. If palms are blessed it is unlawful to
  omit the procession. During the Procession, no station is made, and the knocking on the church
  door is no longer done. The processional cross is carried unveiled.
„ The Asperges is omitted; likewise, the Preparation and the Last Gospel.
„ The blessed palms are held in the hands only during the Procession, and when the Passion and
  Gospel are sung.
„ If a Priest has permission from the Ordinary to celebrate two Masses today, he may omit the
  Passion in one (not the principal) Mass. In this Mass the Priest says the Preparation (omitting the
  Psalm Judica). Normally today's Passion Gospel is read and the Gospel of the Blessing of Palms
  is read as the Last Gospel; but if a Priest has to say more than one Mass, he need only read it at
  one of them; in others he reads the Gospel from the Blessing of Palms.
General Notes for the Sacred Triduum (Post-Schism 1955 Church of Rome rubrics)
„ During the Triduum (revised order), the rules for the Divine Office sung in choir, or recited in com-
  mon, are these: (a) Matins and Lauds (formerly known as Tenebræ) are not anticipated, but said
  in the morning at the appropriate hour. (b) The Little Hours are said at the normal hour. (c) On
  Thursday and Friday, Vespers are omitted, being replaced by the liturgy of the afternoon or even-
  ing, and on Saturday Compline is omitted.
„ The Office on these three days is normally not sung but said or monotoned. At all the Hours
  through None of Holy Saturday, Gloria Patri (“Glory be to the Father”) is omitted at the end of the
  Psalms and in the Responsories. The Chapter, Short Responsory, and Hymn are not said during
  the Triduum.

„ Each Hours concludes with the Antiphon Christus factus est (“Christ for our sake”), Pater in secret,
  the Psalm Miserere in a low voice, and the Collect Concede, quæsumus (“Almighty God, we be-
  seech thee”).
„ During the Triduum, the Martyrology is not read at the end of Prime.
„ At Compline, the Psalms are begun at once; and after the Psalms at once is said the Canticle
  Nunc dimittis; followed by the Antiphon Christus factus est and the rest. On Holy Saturday, Com-
  pline is omitted by those who are to assist at the Easter Vigil rite.
„ The organ may not be played during the Triduum; nor is it permissible to ring bells (traditionally, a
  wooden clapper is used instead).
Notes for Maundy Thursday (Post-Schism 1955 Church of Rome rubrics)
„ Normally, only one Mass is permitted to be celebrated today, and it should be celebrated with all
  possible dignity and solemnity: the best white vestments are worn; the high altar (but this alone)
  adorned with its most costly array; flowers may be used.
„ In the revised rite of Holy Week, this Mass must be celebrated in the evening, i.e. between 4 and
  9 pm.
„ When the Gloria in excelsis is intoned, the Organ is played and the bells rung; after it they are
  silent until the Gloria on Holy Saturday exclusive. (During this time it is customary to use a wooden
  clapper in place of a bell.)57
„ It is recommended that at this Mass today a sermon should be preached, recalling the mystery
  which this day's Mass commemorates, namely the institution of the Blessed Eucharist, and of the
  order of the priesthood, together with our Lord's commandment of brotherly love.
„ The ceremony of the Mandatum, or washing of feet, may take place in the Liturgy, after the Gospel
  (and sermon); the Gospel is not repeated. But if the Mandatum occurs outside Mass, the ceremo-
  nies are preceded by the singing of the Gospel of the Mass (Ante diem festum Paschæ, "Before
  the feast of the Passover").
„ Today, even at Mass celebrated without Deacon and Subdeacon, the Blessed Sacrament must
  be incensed at each Elevation.
„ When the Celebrant consecrates the additional Particles for tomorrow's Communion, he shall,
  according to Orthodox practice, touch each Particle with a tiny amount of the precious Blood.
„ At the end of the function, a priest in surplice and white stole takes the Sacrament reserved for
  the sick to some remote place (it may be the sacristy; or some other seemly chamber outside the
  body of the church), suitably prepared, where It will be kept with a light continuously burning be-
  fore It, until It is brought back at the end of the functions on Holy Saturday.
„ Also, after the function, Holy Water is removed from all fonts in the Church; and a watch is kept
  before the Blessed Sacrament at the altar of repose; it must continue at least until midnight, and
  may laudably be held continuously until the Solemn Liturgy of Good Friday.
„ After the Procession, Vespers are said in Choir with extinguished candles. After Vespers the Altars
  are stripped, only the Cross and the six candlesticks being allowed to remain. This holds good
  likewise for the next day. (But if, in any place, Vespers are not said in Choir, the stripping of the
  Altars takes place immediately after the removal of the Ciborium with the Blessed Sacrament.)
Notes for Good Friday (Post-Schism 1955 Church of Rome rubrics)
„ Today's Solemn Liturgy, according to the revised order, should be celebrated around 3 pm; but it
  may be held at any time between 12 noon and 6 pm, if pastoral reasons make this necessary. In
  the revised rite, the faithful may receive Holy Communion.
„ The bells and organ remain silent until Gloria in excelsis at the Mass on Holy Saturday.
„ The altar Cross is veiled in violet, not black.
„ The Celebrant begins the service in alb and black stole; at the Solemn Collects, he assumes a
  black cope (and the Sacred Ministers black dalmatic and tunicle); these last vestments are re-
  moved at the Adoration of the Cross; and at the distribution of Holy Communion, violet chasuble,
  dalmatic and tunicle are worn.
„ Those who take part in the Solemn Liturgy are dispensed from praying Vespers. But if Vespers are
  to be said in choir, the cross used for the adoration remains on the altar, as also the pair of
  candles (extinguished).

Notes for Holy Saturday (Post-Schism 1955 Church of Rome rubrics)
„ According to the revised order, the ceremonies of the Paschal Vigil take place on Saturday night,
  such that the Mass itself begins around midnight.
„ The faithful may receive Holy Communion. Those who receive at the Vigil Mass may receive again
  the next morning, in the Mass of Easter Day.
„ An abbreviated form of Lauds is sung after the Communion of the people. Those who were present
  at the Vigil Liturgy are dispensed from praying Matins and Lauds.
„ The Celebrant of the Vigil rite takes the ablutions at this Mass as usual; and, notwithstanding this
  and the fact that he has already celebrated Mass, may in addition celebrate one, or even two or
  three Masses on Easter morning.
„ After the rite is ended, the Blessed Sacrament reserved for the sick is brought back into the
  church.
„ If people who are to be baptized are present, especially if there should be many of them, it is
  permissible to transfer to a convenient time in the morning of the same day the ceremonies of
  the Ritual that precede the actual administration of Baptism, namely, in the Baptism of Infants up
  to the word Credis ("Do you believe"), and in the Baptism of Adults up the words Quis vocaris?
  ("What is your name?").
„ The observance of Lenten fasting and abstinence ceases at midnight.
